items.statement: FY27 loan book growth guidance of 26-27% for H1, maintaining 20-25% medium-term growth
items.quote: I would say probably between 26%, 27% growth we should deliver now on a full year basis.

items.statement: FY27 new loan disbursals guidance of 60-62 million
items.quote: We are well on track to deliver between 60 million to 62 million new loans in FY27.

items.statement: FY27 new customer additions guidance of 18-20 million
items.quote: We are clear about adding between 18 MM to 20 MM customers to the franchise in FY27.

items.statement: FY27 fee income growth guidance of 15-18%
items.quote: we should be able to sustain a 15% to 18% fee income growth is what I would just say to you.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost outlook remains in the same corridor as Q2
items.quote: Rest of the year, we should look at it in the same corridor, is what I would just say to you.

items.statement: FY27 opex-to-NTI improvement guidance of 25-40 bps
items.quote: We remain pretty comfortable place to deliver a 25 to 40 basis point improvement in FY27 on opex-to-NTI.

items.statement: FY27 loan loss to average AUF guidance of ~1.32% (excluding macro overlay)
items.quote: Excluding this provision, the loan losses and provisions actually declined year-on-year by 12% and loan loss to average AUF in the process would look to be like 1.32%.

items.statement: FY27 3PL origination target of 3.5% (down from 7%)
items.quote: We have brought that down from 14% to 7% in terms of origination. My mandate to the team is to bring that down to 3.5% in the 6 months' time.

items.statement: Gold loan branches to reach 2,800 by FY27-end
items.quote: we remain quite clear about ending the year with close to 2,800 on stand-alone gold branches.

items.statement: Macro overlay provision of INR 337 crores in Q2 FY27 for resilience
items.quote: we recognized, as I said, a macroeconomic overlay of 337 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan short-tenure schemes discontinued to avoid customer delinquency
items.quote: We have since August stopped doing short-tenor schemes as a firm. We don't see any credit cost impact.

items.statement: New credit card issuances grew **19% QoQ** to **1.4 million** in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: "New credit card issuances at **1.4 million** have grown by nearly **19% quarter-on-quarter**."

items.statement: Cost of funds remained **flat at 4.4%** QoQ due to FCNR deposit mix; no sequential uptick.
items.quote: "Our cost of funds is flat quarter-to-quarter, at about **4.4%** last quarter to this quarter... Sequentially, it has remained flat."

items.statement: Retail consumption growth robust (**30%+** in 2-wheelers, passenger vehicles; **11% YoY** in consumer durables).
items.quote: "Retail consumption growth has also been robust with passenger vehicles, 2-wheeler sales all growing upwards of **30-plus percentage**. Even consumer durables grew at about **11% year-on-year**."

items.statement: ECLGS 5.0 scheme drove **Rs 41,000 cr** in MSME disbursements (highest among banks).
items.quote: "Our ECLGS disbursals of **Rs 41,000 crores** were highest across all banks as of August 26, when the scheme achieved targeted levels."

items.statement: Revised FY27 zinc cost of production guidance downward to $825–$850/ton from earlier $975–$1,000/ton
items.quote: we are revising our COP guidance to $825 to $850 for the full year.

items.statement: Confident of achieving FY27 silver production guidance of 680 tons
items.quote: we are confident we will be able to deliver our guidance of 680.

items.statement: Silver deficit projected at 1.44K tons in 2026; industrial demand rising
items.quote: Silver, again, is expected to remain in deficit for the sixth consecutive year in 2026. The overall shortfall is projected at about 1.44 thousand tons.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 zinc COP at $703/ton (29% better YoY); sulfuric acid byproduct revenue boosts margins
items.quote: zinc cost of production is better by 29%. Our zinc cost of production in second quarter FY27 stands at $703 per ton.

items.statement: Silver production up 20% YoY to 173 tons in Q2; contributed 45% of H1 profitability
items.quote: saleable silver production has risen 20% year-on-year. This stands at 173 tons in this quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, energy disruptions, and tariff policies may drive near-term volatility in commodity prices
items.quote: the global business environment remains challenging amid escalating geopolitical tensions, energy and trade disruptions, changing tariff policies.

items.statement: Exploration for 4 critical mineral blocks (3 exploration, 1 mining lease) to conclude by Q3 FY29; production plans to follow
items.quote: we'll be finishing our exploration program in the third quarter of FY29. So, that will be the time when we will know the exact ore body position and resources available there.

items.statement: NIM to decline marginally in Q3 FY27 due to FCNR(B) impact, then stabilize and rise with current policy rates
items.quote: We do expect a marginal decline in NIM in the current quarter. But after that, we do expect NIM to start increasing even at the current policy rate levels.

items.statement: FCNR(B) impact on NIM estimated at 9-10 bps; CASA ratio decline contributed to margin compression
items.quote: As I did mention, there has been a marginal decline in CASA ratio, and the impact of that mix change between CASA and term deposits has been about nine to ten basis points.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth broad-based (capex, working capital); shift from bond/ECB markets to bank borrowing
items.quote: The growth has been largely broad-based, and it includes segments across capex, and a higher working capital cycle. Yes, there has been some demand shift from bond market, ECBs, towards bank borrowing.

items.statement: Loan growth momentum driven by economic activity, government/RBI policy support; no specific growth targets
items.quote: Loan growth has picked up over the last three or four quarters across segments... This is largely a reflection of the continuing momentum of economic activity as well as impact from very supportive policy measures by government and RBI.

items.statement: Gross NPA additions ₹4,833 cr (₹3,700 cr rural/retail, ₹1,100 cr corporate); net additions ₹1,213 cr after ₹3,620 cr recoveries
items.quote: We have had a gross addition to NPAs of about ₹4,800 crore during the quarter, out of which rural and retail is ₹3,700 crore, and corporate and business banking is about ₹1,100 crore... Against this ₹4,800 crore of gross addition, there has been recoveries and upgrades of ₹3,600 crore.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth to remain strong; shift from bond/offshore markets driving demand
items.quote: Growth is supported currently by some of the factors that we mentioned earlier, including some amount of shift from bond markets as well as some amount of shift from offshore to onshore rupee markets.

items.statement: Margins to stabilize post-Q3; rate hikes to offset FCNR drag
items.quote: From Q4, I would expect margins to come back in a healthy way as these factors start to reverse out, even assuming that there are no further rate hikes.

items.statement: Agricultural provision reversal pending RBI review; update expected in next 2 quarters
items.quote: That process is underway. Hopefully, we should have an update on that over the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: FCNR deposits (~USD 18B) leveraged for loan growth; USD 10B deployed, USD 3.6B via partner banks
items.quote: About USD 18 billion in all, around USD 10 billion where we have provided loans to the customers, about USD 3.6 billion or so where partner banks have provided loans.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth driven by working capital, shift from bond/offshore markets, and investment activity
items.quote: What is driving it, I think, is a mix of factors. Working capital requirements, some shift from bond markets, some shift from foreign currency borrowing markets, and some amount of investment activity.

items.statement: Jewel loans growth constrained by RBI guideline alignment; operational adjustments ongoing
items.quote: The sequential growth has come off as we have been aligning our processes and the distribution as well as various operational risk management measures towards the new RBI guidelines.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain between 0.25-0.30% despite ECL transition impact of ~15 bps.
items.quote: With that, our credit cost still it will remain between 0.25% to 0.30%. So, rest assured that we are very mindful to provide the ROA of more than 1.04%, 1.05%, and the ROE around 15% to 17% minimum it will be there.

items.statement: Recovery target for FY27 set at INR 12,000-13,000 crores, with Q3 expected to reach INR 3,500 crores.
items.quote: I am expecting at least in this quarter, the recovery should happen in the range of around INR 3,500 crores. So we will be trying to reach that figure around INR 13,000 crores figure.

items.statement: Corporate credit sanctions crossed INR 2.5 lakh crores in H1 FY27, with pipeline of INR 1.58 lakh crores.
items.quote: Further, in the first half of this year, we have already crossed more than INR 2.5 lakh crores of sanctions in the corporate credit. Our pipeline credit is to the tune of INR 1.58 lakh crores.

items.statement: Core advances grew 17.4% YoY excluding IBPC impact, with retail (16.3%), MSME (19.8%), and agri (18.1%) leading growth.
items.quote: Excluding this impact, core advances registered a robust Y-o-Y growth of 17.4%, reflecting healthy credit demand and strong underlying business momentum.

items.statement: NII grew 10.8% YoY to INR 11,601 crores, surpassing guidance of 7% sequential growth.
items.quote: NII increased to INR 11,601 crores, registering Y-o-Y growth of 10.8% and sequential growth of 7.4%, surpassing our stated guidance of 7%.

items.statement: Credit demand robust across retail, agri, and MSME segments, with corporate sanctions at INR 4 lakh crores in FY26.
items.quote: Bank sanctioned INR 4 lakh crores in FY 2025-26 in corporate credit lines. Further, in the first half of this year, we have already crossed more than INR 2.5 lakh crores of sanctions in the corporate credit.

items.statement: No material impact from geopolitical tensions; slippages contained, SMA accounts stable, and credit portfolio performing well.
items.quote: We have not seen any material impact of geopolitical tensions on the bank's asset quality. Our slippages remain contained, SMA accounts are stable, and the overall credit portfolio continues to perform well.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 NIM stable vs Q2, Q4 FY27 NIM to improve positively due to repo hike, FCNR deployment, and RIDF run-down.
items.quote: Q3, our expectation is that we should be in the similar range on margins that we've seen compared to Q2, maybe there might be some bias of pulling it back because of the full effect of the FCNR. items.statement: FY28 ROA likely to exceed 1% (vs FY27 guidance of 1%), driven by core ROA improvement and stable asset quality.
items.quote: What we certainly believe is that that core ROA performance, we continue to see a material improvement even in H1. So for example, we've already higher on the core ROA closer to like 20 basis points as we see H1 playing out. And that improvement, we are very confident that we will continue to deliver. So as we go into

items.statement: Growth of 11% in risk-weighted assets possible without capital consumption due to DTA release benefits.
items.quote: So at about, 8.2% accretion to ROE actually in effect allows us, with the benefit of DTA, we have ability to grow at 11% without consuming capital.

items.statement: RIDF deposits to reduce by ₹8,000 crore in H2 FY27 (₹4,500 cr in Q3, ₹3,500 cr in Q4).
items.quote: H2 reduction is expected to be about INR 8,000 crores, H2 and that split Q3 as about INR 4,500 crores and Q4 of about, let's say, INR 3,500 crores.

items.statement: No explicit capex guidance provided; focus on operational efficiency and franchise strengthening.
items.quote: Our priorities remain centered on improving core Profitability, growing Advances and Deposits in a risk-calibrated manner, deepening the granular deposit franchise, managing margins and operating efficiency, and maintaining Asset Quality.

items.statement: Advances grew 23.7% YoY (17.6% ex-FCTL), Retail +35%, Commercial Banking +20.2%, Corporate/Institutional +31.4%.
items.quote: Reported Advances grew by 23.7% year-on-year. Excluding the FCTL linked to the FCNR mobilization, Advances grew 17.6% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 business growth guidance of 14-15% exceeded at 20.54%. Deposit growth guidance of 10-12% exceeded at 14.41%. Advances growth guidance of 14-16% exceeded at 29.83%. CASA guidance of 48±1% missed at 44.65%.
items.quote: "We have given guidance for business growth 14% to 15% and we have achieved 20.54%, in deposit growth our guidance was 10% to 12% and we have achieved 14.41%, in advances growth our guidance was 14% to 16% and we have achieved 29.83%. CASA guidance was 48% plus or minus 1%. Here, due to obvious reason, due to FCNR(B) m

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance of <2.5% met at 2.39%. Net NPA guidance of improvement maintained at 0.31%.
items.quote: "Gross NPA stood at 2.39% that is also aligned with our guidance given to the market that it will be below 2.50%. Net NPA stood at 0.31%, also there is an improvement of 17-basis points and that is also in alliance with our guidance to the market."

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agriculture, MSME) book grew 21.11% YoY to Rs.2,54,273 Crores. Retail grew 24.49%, Agriculture 19.92%, MSME 17.36%.
items.quote: "RAM sector was 21%. We reached the level of Rs.2,54,273 Crores and within which retail has grown by 24.49%, agriculture has grown by approximately 20%, MSME has grown by approximately 17%."

items.statement: Management expects deal closure by Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27, with Nagarro integration taking 5-6 months post-close.
items.quote: We expect the deal closure by Q4-CY26 or Q1-CY27. We will keep you posted on the progress of this over time.

items.statement: Management aims for EBIT margins of 16-17% over time, with growth driving profitability.
items.quote: We want to be in the 16 to 17% range, that is our aspiration. That will be our endeavour.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 TCV stood at USD 633.5M, with new bookings of USD 367.1M and ACV of USD 481M (new ACV: USD 262.3M).
items.quote: The total contract value for the quarter stood at USD 633.5 million, with total contract value of new bookings coming in at USD 367.1 million. The annual contract value of bookings for this quarter was USD 481 million, out of which the annual contract value from new bookings contributed to USD 262.3 million.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month TCV growth of 36.3%, ACV growth of 21.9%.
items.quote: If I look at that TTM year on year, the trailing 12 months, the TCV growth is 36.3%. If I look at the ACV growth on a TTM basis, it is 21.9%.

items.statement: EBIT margin declined 100 bps QoQ to 15% due to wage hikes, lower utilization, and large deal amortization.
items.quote: EBIT margins for Q2 FY27 came in at 15%, 130 basis points declined year-on-year.

items.statement: Large deal amortization impact (~90 bps) expected to reduce as revenue scales and optimization kicks in.
items.quote: The plan is to leverage FinOps and AI-led engineering roadmap to optimize the spend across people, tools, and cloud infrastructure in this large deal going forward. As we optimize the spend and our revenue scales in future, the impact on our margins will gradually reduce.

items.statement: Wage hike impacted margins by 140 bps net (180 bps headwind partially offset by lower ESOP costs).
items.quote: This impacted our margins by 180 basis points. However, lower ESOP costs enabled us to absorb part of this impact, leaving us with a net impact of 140 basis points.

items.statement: Large deal includes third-party licenses and cloud spend amortization (~USD 4M), reducing margins temporarily.
items.quote: This investment in the third-party tools and licenses led to an increase in the quarterly amortization of approximately USD 4 million.

items.statement: BFSI demand driven by vendor consolidation, AI modernization, and legacy platform upgrades.
items.quote: Vendor consolidation in pockets is still a big thing. Second is the modernization side of it, whether it is the data modernization play, getting the financial services institutions ready for the AI part.

items.statement: Nagarro acquisition one-time expenses (~USD 50M) spread over 3-4 quarters, impacting EPS.
items.quote: We are expecting one-time expenses to the tune of approximately $50 million spread over three to four quarters. These expenses will weigh in on the reported EPS growth.

items.statement: USD 1.25B funding planned (USD 450M equity, rest debt/equity-linked instruments) for Nagarro acquisition.
items.quote: We will be raising USD 1.25 billion in terms of both debt and equity. Out of this, USD 450 million will be raised through equity.

items.statement: Investing in tech/product/brand despite slower trading; long-term growth focus
items.quote: we choose to keep investing in technology, product, and brands even though trading activity was slower across the board.

items.statement: Capitalized INR 62M on app rebuild; payback over several years
items.quote: During this quarter, we capitalized about INR 62 million of costs on this build, and we expect to pay it off over the next several years.

items.statement: Customer growth strong; 95% DIY account openings this quarter
items.quote: more than 95% of customers who joined us this quarter opened their accounts completely on their own, which is in a DIY fashion.

items.statement: India added 16M demat accounts in H1; long-term bullish on retail participation
items.quote: India added roughly 16 million demat accounts in the first half, and domestic funds and households continue to own the largest share of listed companies.

items.statement: Net profit INR 7.1 crore; lower YoY due to tech/product investments
items.quote: Net Profit was INR 7.1 crore, lower than Q1, because we choose to keep investing in technology, product, and brands.

items.statement: Mutual fund assets on platform at INR 2,095 crore
items.quote: Mutual fund assets on our platform now are at INR 2,095 crores.

items.statement: Soft market quarter; derivatives volume dropped post-cash rollout
items.quote: Derivatives volume dropped after the cash rollout, and active NSE clients stayed at about 46 million overall.

items.statement: Rights issue strengthened balance sheet; net worth now INR 1,136 crore
items.quote: Our net worth now is INR 11,360 million, or INR 1,136 crores, compared with INR 650 crores at the end of March 2026.

items.statement: HDFC Life expects FY27 growth in line with industry, with broad-based channel momentum continuing.
items.quote: We expect to sustain this momentum and grow in line with the industry in FY27.

items.statement: Non-par savings and annuity mix to remain elevated due to interest rate environment.
items.quote: With interest rates at elevated levels, this is an opportune time for customers to lock in long-term guaranteed returns.

items.statement: Bancassurance partnerships grew 13% YoY in Q2, including new J&K Bank partnership.
items.quote: Other bancassurance partnerships also grew well, delivering a YoY growth of 13% in Q2.

items.statement: Retail protection policies grew 33% in H1, with 2-year CAGR of 30%.
items.quote: Retail protection grew 33% in H1, a two-year CAGR of 30%.

items.statement: Credit protect grew 19% in H1, broad-based across portfolios.
items.quote: Credit protect grew 19% in H1, with growth broad-based across portfolios.

items.statement: Ibuprofen breakeven in Q2 FY27, but profitability uncertain next quarters due to macroeconomic factors
items.quote: "Will we get back to the earlier days when we had INR10 crores, INR15 crores loss, It's very difficult to say that at this time. But I can tell you that the general health of the ibuprofen business has improved as well. But in this particular instance, it's more macroeconomic conditions that's driving the breakeven."

items.statement: Base business revenue growth of 37% YoY to INR 327 crores, EBITDA margin at 23.6% (up 440 bps YoY)
items.quote: "Revenue grew 37% year-on-year to INR 327 crores, staying above the INR 300 crores number for the third quarter in a row. EBITDA grew 68% to INR77 crores, with the margin up about 440 basis points to 23.6%."

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 18.4% (up 720 bps YoY) due to gross margin improvement and flat operating costs
items.quote: "Our overall EBITDA margin expanded to 18.4% from 11% around last year and it is a significant improvement of roughly 720 basis points as compared to Y-o-Y."

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 500+ crores (from INR 614 crores in March '26) via rights issue and operational cash flows
items.quote: "We have been able to reduce net debt to close to INR500-odd crores from INR614-odd crores, which was there as on March '26."

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA ratio improved to 1.8x (from 3.2x last year) and aims to sustain medium-term
items.quote: "Considering the H1 Annualised EBITDA, the Net Debt to EBITDA ratio multiple has actually improved to close to 1.8x as compared to 3.2x what we had last year."

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing raw material availability challenges and pricing pressures
items.quote: "We continue to face pricing pressures and raw material availability challenges, which led to intermittent production stoppages. But despite that, I think we recorded a good set of numbers."

items.statement: Solar bid pipeline (excluding BESS) grew to 34 GW (74% India, 26% overseas) from 27.7 GW last quarter.

items.quote: The moderation in margin reflects our continued investment in sales, strategy and new growth areas to support the next phase of growth. Importantly, despite these investments, our underlying profitability remains healthy.

items.statement: Margins to improve post-FY27 as investments absorb; FY28 EBITDA margin target: double-digit.
items.quote: For FY28 onwards it will be there double-digit, and for this year I said it will be 9 to 10 here.

items.statement: Box build revenue grew 86% YoY; shift toward higher-value integration solutions.

items.statement: Strong demand across aerospace (62% YoY growth), industrial (29%), defense (13%), and Medtech (14%).
items.quote: Revenue grew 26.5% year-on-year in Q2, supported by strong growth in aerospace and industrial together with the continued traction in defense and Medtech.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY; order book supports visibility for H2.

items.statement: Investments in sales, marketing, and product development (e.g., B2S) to drive long-term growth.

items.statement: No full-service urban branches added in Q2; focus on gold loan and rural loan branches.

items.statement: Retail 90+ delinquency stable at 0.7%; credit cost at multiyear lows (1.5% in Q2).

items.quote: We have already done 6 capex in last 6 years, that is amounting to roughly INR500 crores. And that all has been funded by ourselves.

items.statement: Export revenue at 80% of total; domestic at 20%. SCF: 51%, PPF: 24%, IPD: 25%.
items.quote: This quarter our export was 80% and domestic was 20%. So it's a 51% from sun control, 24% from PPF, and balance around 25% from IPD.

items.statement: Architectural films contribute 30% of window film sales (~INR400 crores annualized).
items.quote: Presently, like I said, it is a very good success story for us. We started with 10%. Today, we are roughly 30% of our sales is coming from architectural business, from window films.

items.statement: TPU backward integration expected to add 1.5-2% to EBITDA margins in FY28.
items.quote: We will add once the TPU comes on stream, and it starts contributing to PPF, overall company revenue should go up by these numbers. That is, you are right, 27 plus-minus plus 1.5 to 2.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue mix: 73% CPD, 27% IPD; value-added products at 86%.
items.quote: Our H1 revenue mix comprised 73% from CPD and 27% from IPD, while value-added products accounted for 86% of revenue.

items.statement: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin improvement of 100-150 bps annually despite inflationary pressures.
items.quote: we'd like to maintain that, which would be around 100 to 150 basis points improvement in profitability year-on-year.

items.statement: Capex per store ranges INR3-3.5 crore; FY27 capex expected INR250-300 crore.
items.quote: our capex will be within the range of INR250 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 10.1% driven by double-digit guest count growth.
items.quote: same-store sales also grew at a double-digit 10.1%.

items.statement: Guest count grew double-digit every month in Q2 FY27, driven by value strategy.
items.quote: guest count grew in double digits in each month of this quarter.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA grew 29% YoY with margin expansion of 130 bps to 13.1%.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA grew 29% year-on-year with margins expanding by 130 basis points to 13.1%.

items.statement: Inflation absorbed 190 bps; 50% of inflation passed via pricing, rest via cost savings.
items.quote: we take a price increase to absorb half of inflation in terms of the pressures that we see as a principle.

items.statement: Strong consumer demand with broad-based growth across West and South regions.
items.quote: growth was driven by more customers choosing McDonald's more often.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue growth guidance upgraded to 15-18% YoY, EBITDA margin 13.8-14.3%.
items.quote: Based on the strong half-year performance and the visibility we see across our customer portfolio, we have increased our FY27 outlook. We now expect revenue growth of 15% to 18% for FY27 and an EBITDA margin in the range of 13.8% to 14.3%.

items.statement: 3-year digital engineering contract renewal worth ~INR44.5 cr, 70% higher than prior term.
items.quote: A major highlight this quarter was the renewal of a 3-year digital engineering engagement valued at approximately INR44.5 crores with a global construction and mining equipment leader. The contract value increased by over 70% compared to the previous term.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 15.6% in Q2 FY27, driven by higher utilization and offshore leverage.
items.quote: EBITDA grew 33.7% year-on-year to INR26.6 crores, with margins expanding to all-time high at 15.6%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance revised upward; ARR now ~78 cr, expects >75 cr executable order book
items.quote: "FY27, our current order book is at INR 78 crores, which is the executable order book. It should be above INR 75 crores for sure."

items.statement: ARR expected to reach ~120 cr by FY28 Q3 if Q3/Q4 CapEx deployed
items.quote: "From December month, FY27 to FY28 Q3, you'll be able to see that our ARR has gone up to even INR 120 crores."

items.statement: Peak revenue potential of ~300 cr post INR 1,000 cr gross block by FY29/FY30
items.quote: "We can talk around INR 300 crores worth of revenues easily."

items.statement: INR 400 cr CapEx program for FY25-FY27 completed 90% (~INR 370 cr deployed)
items.quote: "We have now deployed approximately INR 370 crores worth of assets, inclusive of GST, achieving more than 90% of our program."

items.statement: Mission 2030: INR 1,000 cr gross block by FY30, 20% allocated to wind energy
items.quote: "We are setting our sights on Mission 2030. This is our long-term management objective to build Trishakti's cumulative gross block to more than INR 1,000 crores by FY30."

items.statement: INR 600-700 cr CapEx planned for next 3 years (FY28-FY30) based on demand visibility
items.quote: "Another INR 600-700 crores of CapEx can easily be done in the next three years on a blended way, by seeing the last three years' demand."

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable at 60.89% in Q2 FY27, no YoY/QoQ decline expected
items.quote: "Our EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 60.89%."

items.statement: Machine pricing stable in India; global arbitrage possible for higher-tonnage machines
items.quote: "In India, the rental yields are stable. If we increase the machine pricing, then, obviously, either the rental yield has to go up. Since the rental yield has the same, the pricing of the machine in India are going to be constant only."

items.statement: High demand in Gujarat/Odisha due to infrastructure/industrial CapEx; 100% fleet utilization
items.quote: "If we want to do a lot of CapEx, then these are the two places which are currently having many, many number of new plants coming up."

items.statement: Demand visibility from Reliance, L&T, Tata Steel, and other blue-chip clients for 5-6 years
items.quote: "Majority of the mega companies in India are having their Phase 1 and Phase 2 plan set up in this financial year. If they are starting those jobs, all are five-year, six-year contracts."

items.statement: Debt repayment priority; net debt expected to peak at INR 400-500 cr, then decline post-FY28
items.quote: "We feel that our net debt should not cross more than INR 400-500 crores on the long-term basis."

items.statement: Debt preferred over equity; equity dilution only if debt funding becomes difficult
items.quote: "First priority is to share in debt, of course, and that is only cheaper than equity. If that is a concern, then equity is the only option."

items.statement: India market demand robust but slowing in next quarters as GST cuts fade; tractor growth slower than other segments
items.quote: We expect a relative slowing down in market growth over the next few quarters as the effect of GST cuts diminish.

items.statement: Book growth CAGR of 20%+ over Lakshya 2031 period
items.quote: We had set ourselves a book growth CAGR of 20%+ over the Lakshya period.

items.statement: Credit cost target of 2% or less over Lakshya 2031 period
items.quote: We continue to drive credit costs down to a level of 2% or less over the Lakshya period.

items.statement: RoA target of 3.0%-3.2% by FY31
items.quote: Our Return on Assets (RoA) target remains in the range of 3.0%-3.2% for FY31.

items.statement: Gold loan book grew 242% YoY to ₹5,043 Cr in Q2FY27
items.quote: The closing book reached ₹5,043 Cr at the end of the quarter, representing a significant growth of 242% YoY.

items.statement: Rural book grew 22% YoY to ₹33,465 Cr in Q2FY27
items.quote: The book size reached ₹33,465 Cr, up by 22% YoY in Q2FY27.

items.statement: Urban finance book grew 32% YoY to ₹67,668 Cr in Q2FY27
items.quote: The overall Urban Finance book size increased to ₹67,668 Cr in Q2FY27, translating into a 32% YoY growth.

items.statement: Credit cost moderated to 2.46% in Q2FY27 (down 8 bps QoQ)
items.quote: Credit cost has moderated to 2.46% this quarter, reflecting a further sequential improvement of 8 bps from 2.54% in Q1FY27.

items.statement: NIMs+Fees stable at 10.48% in Q2FY27 (vs. 10.47% in Q1FY27)
items.quote: Our NIMs + Fees, which is another focus area for us, stood stable at 10.48% against 10.47% in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Rural disbursements attenuated in drought-affected regions (Karnataka, Maharashtra, AP, Telangana)
items.quote: We have been cognizant of this early on. And in our underwriting parameters, some of the guardrails have been strengthened in all these districts.

items.statement: Lakshya 2031 RoA target of 3%–3.2% remains achievable despite insurance commission risks.
items.quote: we are reasonably confident that our stated objective of Lakshya 2031, which is delivering an RoA profile of 3% to 3.2% will be met.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to stay within 2%–2.2% corridor by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: we are very confident of hitting that 2% to 2.2% corridor of credit cost as promised in Q4FY27.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio (C/I) below 40% (currently ~39%), target further reduction.
items.quote: Cost-to-income ratio right now is about 39%. And it has fallen below 40%. Our objective is to drive it down further downwards.

items.statement: Gold loans AUM to reach ₹40,000–45,000 Cr (~14%–15% of total AUM) by Lakshya 2031.
items.quote: we want Gold Loans AUM to hit about 14% to 15% of our overall AUM by the end of Lakshya 2031, which is Gold Loan AUM between ₹40,000 Cr to ₹45,000 Cr.

items.statement: Personal loans disbursements to grow sequentially to ₹1,700–1,800 Cr/month post-Cyclops calibration.
items.quote: We intend to take it in interim to about ₹1,700 Cr, ₹1,700 Cr to ₹1,800 Cr before we calibrate.

items.statement: NIMs + fees to remain in mid-range of 10%–10.5% (10.25% target).
items.quote: NIMs plus fees is expected to be in that mid-range of 10% to 10.5%, which is 10.25%.

items.statement: Gold loan branches to expand to 2,000 (from 800 by FY-end), then consolidate.
items.quote: we have a plan of expanding until about 2,000 branches, right, post which we'll probably take a pause.

items.statement: Yields maintained via risk-based pricing; no erosion despite prime customer shift.
items.quote: we are able to clearly segment the customer and the risk-based pricing is absolutely being working on the full portfolio.

items.statement: Confident of exceeding 10 GWh battery storage target for FY27 due to accelerated deployment.
items.quote: we are very committed to not only commission the 10 gigawatt by the end of the year, but would be definitely able to surpass it too. But yes, we are very confident of achieving it and also surpassing it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin remains industry-leading at 92-93% (Q2: 92%, H1: 93%) despite curtailment.
items.quote: EBITDA from power supply ending 51% higher Y-o-Y to INR3,835 crores, resulting in a strong EBITDA margin of 92% during the quarter.

items.statement: AI/data centers and industrial growth driving firm/dispatchable renewable demand; BESS mitigates curtailment risks.
items.quote: significant opportunities emerging from growing needs for firm and dispatchable renewable energy, rising power demand from AI, data centers and hyperscalers.

items.statement: BESS now accounts for >50% of India’s operational capacity; 10.8 GW solar/wind/hybrid commissioned at Khavda.
items.quote: we commissioned 3 gigawatt hour of battery energy storage at Khavda, taking our total installed storage capacity to 6.6 gigawatt hour. This capacity accounts for more than 50% of India's operational BESS.

items.statement: Revised FY27 profitability guidance: ROA 5.2%-5.8% (up from 4%-4.8%), ROE 21%-24% (up from 16%-20%).
items.quote: Basis our strong H1 FY27 financial performance, we raised our profitability guidance for FY27, ROA of 5.2% to 5.8% versus 4% to 4.8% earlier and ROE of 21% to 24% versus 16% to 20% earlier.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance retained at 20%-25% YoY, driven by Group Loan recovery and Retail Finance momentum.
items.quote: We retain our AUM growth guidance of 20% to 25%, supported by return to growth in Group Loan portfolio, coupled with continued momentum in Retail Finance.

items.statement: NIM guidance revised to 14.4%-14.7% (up from 12.8%-13.2%), driven by asset quality and capital strength.
items.quote: We expect a NIM of 14.4% to 14.7% as against 12.8% to 13.2% guided earlier, driven by healthy asset quality, strong control over borrowing costs and a higher capital position.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected at 29%-30%, despite inflationary trends.
items.quote: Cost to income may range between 29% to 30% as operating costs remain well under control, despite inflationary trends.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 3%-4%, with Q3/Q4 slight uptick expected but within range.
items.quote: We're maintaining our credit cost guidance of 3% to 4%, and it should comfortably cover for any volatility on account of evolving drought-related conditions.

items.statement: 50-bps lending rate cut implemented in Q3 FY27, with another 50-bps planned for Q4 FY27 if credit costs stable.
items.quote: We will do a 50-bps cut this quarter and probably 50-bps in the next quarter. The marginal cost of borrowing increase is slightly because of the mix of borrowing.

items.statement: Marginal cost of borrowing at 9.1% in Q2 FY27, expected to stay in 9.2%-9.3% range till March FY28.
items.quote: Our borrowing cost will stay in this 9.2% to 9.3% range till March.

items.statement: Group Loan book growth to return to guided levels in H2 FY27 post write-offs and seasonal strength.
items.quote: With write-offs normalizing and the seasonally stronger second half ahead and increase in customer acquisition during H2, we expect the Group Loan book growth to return to guided levels.

items.statement: Customer acquisition momentum expected to accelerate in H2 FY27, targeting >1 Lakh new borrowers/month.
items.quote: We are hoping that Q3 and Q4, we should actually see momentum in customers. Ideally, we would like to publish more than 1 Lakh customers every month.

items.statement: Drought-related risks in 6 districts of Maharashtra (central region), with borrowers seeking restructuring; no material impact elsewhere.
items.quote: We are seeing a few signs of drought-related challenges in October around certain pockets of Maharashtra, wherein the borrowers are requesting for additional time for repayment, including restructuring options.

items.statement: Credit cost may inch up in Q3/Q4 due to drought and festivals, but FY27 guidance of 3%-4% remains intact.
items.quote: Right now, what we are saying is that even if we budget a certain amount of increase because of the drought situation, we don't see it go beyond our guidance in this entire year.

items.statement: USD 175M ECB raised at competitive pricing (October 2026), diversifying funding mix and extending tenure.
items.quote: We signed USD 175 million ECB loan in October, syndicated by Standard Chartered Bank and DBS Bank.

items.statement: INR 940 Crore domestic NCDs mobilized via private placement in FY27.
items.quote: We also mobilized INR 940 Crore of domestic NCDs through private placement process in this financial year.

items.statement: Promoters in active discussions for strategic investor at HoldCo level; progress expected in next 2 quarters.
items.quote: Currently, the promoters are in active discussion for a strategic investor as the whole group. That is where it is. And we should see some progress in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 same-store sales growth (SSSG) expected to be >10% to achieve double-digit full-year growth.
items.quote: Q3 will have to be higher than 10%, as you rightly said, for the first nine months to look like double-digit growth.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 SSSG target is double-digit.
items.quote: our goal is to achieve double-digit for the full year.

items.statement: Belong & Co. pilot (apparel format) shows strong early traction; conversion >50%, repeat purchases observed.
items.quote: our conversion of footfall into the store into purchase is north of 50%. So, it's very, very encouraging.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY27 revised upwards due to strong order inflow; no specific number given.
items.quote: "we are seeing increased order inflow from all sorts of customers in India also and abroad also and that's the reason our numbers are much more than what we were originally targeting."

items.statement: Revenue target of INR900-1,000 crores for combined units by FY30-31.
items.quote: "Put together, we see that the Unit 1 and Unit 2 would be able to invoice close to INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores of bushings as a combination of Unit 1 and Unit 2."

items.statement: Order book stands at INR760 crores, up from INR400 crores at start of FY27.
items.quote: "our order book stands at INR760 crores, up from INR400 crores at the start of the financial year."

items.statement: Order book execution expected over next 15-18 months.
items.quote: "The order book is expected to be executed over the next 15 to 18 months."

items.statement: Export order book is INR40-50 crores (5-7% of total).
items.quote: "Maybe 5% to 7% today. INR40-odd crores, INR40 crores to INR50 crores today."

items.statement: Total capex for greenfield project is INR220 crores, INR106 crores spent by H1 FY27.
items.quote: "The total capex planned for the greenfield project is INR220 crores, of which INR106 crores is spent till 30th September '26."

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 28.1% in H1 FY27 from 23.3% in H1 FY26.
items.quote: "EBITDA margin improved from 23.3% to 28.1% year-on-year."

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 48.3% in H1 FY27 from 42.4% in H1 FY26.
items.quote: "Gross margin for H1 FY27 was 48.3% compared with 42.4% in H1 of previous year."

items.statement: Cost savings from localization expected to be 18-20% on import duty and freight.
items.quote: "The cost saving, the import duty and the freight put together is today, say, 18% to 20%."

items.statement: Price realization and product mix contributed to margin improvement.
items.quote: "Product mix and operating leverage, which is a combination of volume increase of close to 40%, better price realization, and cost efficiency measures, were the main contributors."

items.statement: Strong demand from grid modernization, renewable energy, and data centers.
items.quote: "The global power transmission and distribution industry continues to witness structural demand drivers, including grid modernization, replacement of aging infrastructure, renewable energy integration, and rising electricity consumption."

items.statement: RIP bushings accounted for 86% of revenue by value in H1 FY27.
items.quote: "RIP bushings accounted for 86% of the revenue, while OIP and high-current bushings contributed to 14%."

items.statement: Maintain same revenue run rate of ~106% YoY for FY27-FY28; Q3-Q4 typically stronger than Q1-Q2.
items.quote: we are planning to and we have a pipeline to maintain the same run rate. But to make better than this requires a lot of extra efforts. But going forward, we keep trying to maintain the same run rate.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs. 78 crores as of September 30, 2026.
items.quote: So, as on date, the size number based on 31st, 30th September is Rs. 78 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for ZeroTouch expected at 50-60%+ due to proprietary tech; CapEx-heavy product.
items.quote: it is a very good marginable product. More than 50%-60% plus EBITDA margin we have into the ZeroTouch.

items.statement: ZeroTouch demand strong; Q3 FY27 revenue expected to rise due to ongoing exams.
items.quote: Q3, we are expecting a good amount of revenues as our exam is already started from this month.

items.statement: ZeroTouch demand growing; government focus (exams, competitive tests) prioritized over private sector.
items.quote: we are planning to expand according to the current scenarios what we are getting response from our existing client and the new client.

items.statement: ZeroTouch revenue contribution to top line expected at 20-22% in next 2 years.
items.quote: our expectation in the next 2 years of line from ZeroTouch, we are expecting 20-22% revenue will be contributing by ZeroTouch.

items.statement: ZeroTouch currently generating nominal revenue; scaling in government exams (e.g., Gujarat G3Q).
items.quote: we have started our revenue from ZeroTouch. It is, as of now, it is a very nominal stage.
